mission: Propose the exact route or label split for the five form numbers in data/rcap-grade-a/route-obligation-census-v1/source-custody-reconciliation.json ambiguousFormNumbers, which each name more than one distinct document.
nothingWasEdited: This lane edited no worklist, no census, no queue, no manifest, no ledger and no resolver. It wrote exactly one file, this one. Every edit below is a proposal for Captain, because a route change needs a task that authorizes that exact route change (AGENTS.md, 'Roger Approval Required' and 'Do not change live RCAP routes unless a task explicitly authorizes that exact route change').

theOneThingToReadFirst.finding: The five ambiguous form numbers are not one problem. ONE of them costs an obligation and FOUR of them cost nothing.
theOneThingToReadFirst.measured: Simulating the reconciler's tier 1 and tier 2 against all 821 official-form obligations in the worklist: exactly four route obligations, in two families, both Montana, name a label that normalises to an ambiguous form number. No obligation anywhere reaches TX-GC-411.0727, TX-GC-411.0728, TX-GC-411.0729 or TX-GC-411.0731 at either tier. Texas already names the order and the petition under two separate descriptive labels and both already bind at tier 3 to the correct distinct bytes.
theOneThingToReadFirst.soTheProposalIs: Split ONE label — MT-OCA-MMRTA — into two, in both Montana MMRTA families, and add the two tier-3 identity findings that make the new labels bind. Propose NO route change and NO label change for Texas: the four Texas numbers are ambiguous in the corpus index only, the refusal is uncontested, and touching them would change routes for no gain.
theOneThingToReadFirst.andACaution: A label change alone does not resolve anything. The reconciler's tier 1 matches the census label against the CORPUS's form number, and both Montana documents carry form number MT-OCA-MMRTA in the index. 'MT-OCA-MMRTA-ORDER' fails tier 1 (normalised strings differ) and fails tier 2 (the token 'order' is not in the corpus form number's tokens). The split must be paired with either two tier-3 identity findings or a corpus re-index that carries the library's document_role. Step 2 below is not optional garnish.

rootCause.statement: The Master Library never gave two documents one identity. It gave them one document_id and separated them by document_role, and it publishes a composite key that already distinguishes them.
evidence: STATES/MT/STATE_MANIFEST.csv row: asset_class source_gated, document_role ORDER, document_id MT-OCA-MMRTA, workflow_key 'MT:MT-OCA-MMRTA:ORDER:EN', sha256 2e38c3c680bc1c10932e017472a39e676ae4a7ad89621790b20a9803b548db7e.

rootCause.whatTheIndexKeeps: data/rcap-all50/local-source-corpus-index.json carries `assetClass`, which is the SECOND field of the six-field FILENAME (FORM / INSTRUCTIONS / SOURCE-GATED / SUPPORT), and `formNumber`, which is the document_id. It does not carry document_role and it does not carry workflow_key. So the library's own discriminator is dropped at index time, and both Texas siblings arrive as assetClass FORM at one form number, and both Montana siblings arrive as assetClass SOURCE-GATED at one form number.
rootCause.consequence: scripts/lib/official-form-asset-class.mjs can prefer FORM over INSTRUCTIONS and EN over other languages because the index carries assetClass and language. It cannot prefer ORDER over SERVICE or PETITION, because the index carries neither. Its own header says exactly this and refuses, which is correct.

theMeasurement.method: Re-implemented the reconciler's normalise() and tokens() and its tier-1 and tier-2 predicates, then ran every official-form: obligation in data/rcap-grade-a/route-obligation-census-candidate/packet-family-build-worklist.json against the five ambiguous form numbers.
theMeasurement.correctionToTheBriefing: The briefing says five obligations across several families are unresolved. Measured, it is two obligations across two families, both Montana, appearing on four routes because the worklist replicates one family-level requiredSourceIds union onto every route in the family. The other four ambiguous form numbers cost zero obligations. That is not a smaller version of the same problem; it is a different problem with a different fix.

proposal.shape: Two labels, not a split of one. Replace one label with two in both families; every route in both families carries both.

step1_worklistLabelSplit.whyThoseTwoSuffixes: ORDER and SERVICE are not this lane's invention. They are the exact document_role values the Master Library manifest prints for these two rows, and the exact officialFormDocumentRole values the two composed-route dependency.json files already carry. Nothing new has to be agreed for a reader to know which is which.
step1_worklistLabelSplit.alternativeIfCaptainPrefersTheLibraryKey: official-form:MT:MT-OCA-MMRTA:ORDER:EN and official-form:MT:MT-OCA-MMRTA:SERVICE:EN, which are the library's published workflow_key strings. Rejected as the primary proposal only because no other label in the worklist has that shape, and because the reconciler's tokens() would reduce the jurisdiction and language segments to noise.
step1_worklistLabelSplit.gainsOrReplaces: REPLACES one entry with two, in each of the four routes. Each route's requiredSourceIds grows by exactly one: the two mt_mmrta_serving routes go 16 -> 17 entries and the two mt_mmrta_completed routes go 17 -> 18 (counted first-hand in the worklist). documentSourcesNamed on each family's reconciliation row goes 7 -> 8.

step2_makeTheNewLabelsBind.whyItIsMandatory: Tier 1 compares the census label to the corpus's form number, and the corpus form number for BOTH documents is MT-OCA-MMRTA. normalise('MT-OCA-MMRTA-ORDER') = 'mtocammrtaorder' ≠ 'mtocammrta', so tier 1 misses. Tier 2 requires every label token to appear in the corpus form number's tokens; tokens('MT-OCA-MMRTA-ORDER') = ['oca','mmrta','order'] and tokens('MT-OCA-MMRTA') = ['oca','mmrta'], so 'order' is absent and tier 2 refuses. Without step 2 the split turns one 'label_does_not_identify_a_document' into two, and the two families stay SOURCE_IDENTITY_UNRESOLVED.
step2_makeTheNewLabelsBind.add: One entry for familyId mt_mmrta_serving-set and one for mt_mmrta_completed-set, or one entry carrying both artifacts with servesFamilies naming both — the tier-3 loader reads artifacts, not families, unless labelIsFamilySpecific is set.
step2_makeTheNewLabelsBind.doNotSetLabelIsFamilySpecific: Both families need the same two documents at the same two hashes, so these are global label identities, not family-scoped ones. Setting labelIsFamilySpecific would withhold the labels from the global map for no reason.

notForThisLane.theDurableFix: The five ambiguities all exist because the corpus indexer drops the Master Library's document_role. An indexer that carried it — emitting formNumber 'MT-OCA-MMRTA-ORDER'/'MT-OCA-MMRTA-SERVICE' and 'TX-GC-411.0727-ORDER'/'TX-GC-411.0727-PETITION', or carrying documentRole as its own field that preferOfficialForm can discriminate on — would make all five resolve at tier 1 and would make ambiguousFormNumbers empty.
whyItIsNotProposedAsTheEdit: It changes data/rcap-all50/local-source-corpus-index.json, which every lane in this factory reads, and it is not the least change that fixes the measured defect.

It does NOT on its own fix Montana. The worklist would still say official-form:MT-OCA-MMRTA, which would then match NO corpus form number at all and would degrade from label_does_not_identify_a_document to named_form_number_not_in_corpus — an acquisition task for two documents already held. The worklist label split in step 1 is required either way.
It touches no Texas obligation, because no Texas obligation depends on tier 1 for these numbers.
notForThisLane.recommendation: Apply step 1 and step 2 for Montana now. Treat the indexer change as a separate, later, factory-wide task with its own re-run of every consumer, not as part of this split.

whatICouldNotSettle.detail: In both Montana families, requiredSourceIds is a single family-level union replicated verbatim onto every route — the court-petition route and the DOJ CRISS-submission route carry byte-identical lists.
